ITQAN:v2p364/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p364/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p364/r11.claim: كأن لم يغنوا means as though they had never existed; Labid's phrase غنيت سبتا is cited as evidence.
ITQAN:v2p364/r11.anchor: قال كأن لم يكونوا أما سمعت قول لبيد

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r19.claim: The narrative recounts the destruction of Shuʿayb's people after their rejection of him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.claim: The promised messenger mission continued, and the accounts of those messengers are set out in verses 59–92.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p53/.anchor: Then in accordance with this promise, He continued to send messengers. Its details are stated in verses 59-92 ahead.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.claim: Section VI reinforces warnings of the Hereafter to Quraysh with Arabian nations’ histories: they received political authority, became ungrateful and unjust, rejected messengers and were destroyed after respite. Quraysh face the same situation and impending judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p56/.anchor: The purpose of narrating these anecdotes to the Quraysh is that they too are facing the same situation and their fate is about to be decided by God’s court of justice

STUDYQURAN:7:91/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r1.claim: The account of Midian's destruction matches the account of the Thamūd, the people of Ṣāliḥ.
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r1.anchor: The description of the destruction of the Midianites is identical to that of the Thamūd

STUDYQURAN:7:91/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r3.claim: The earthquake erased Midian so completely that it seemed they had never lived there.
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r3.anchor: The people of Midian were so thoroughly effaced by the earthquake that it was as though they had never dwelt there

STUDYQURAN:7:91/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r4.claim: Against the disbelievers' claim that Shuʿayb's followers were losers, the passage declares the disbelievers deluded about true religion and destroyed.
STUDYQURAN:7:91/r4.anchor: In response to the Midianite disbelievers’ description of Shuʿayb’s followers as the losers in v. 90

TAB-FULL:v10p325/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r1.claim: God destroyed Shuʿayb’s deniers and left their town empty, as if they had never settled or lived there.
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r1.anchor: يقال: غني فلان بمكان كذا فهو يغنى به غنى وغنيا

TAB-FULL:v10p325/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r2.claim: The verb ghaniya bi-makān means to dwell or be in a place; the anonymous verse using yaghni and Ruʾba’s maghnā illustrate the usage and derivation.

TAB-FULL:v10p325/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as if they had never lived there or enjoyed life there.
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r3.anchor: كأن لم يعيشوا، كأن لم ينعموا

TAB-FULL:v10p325/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that they seemed never to have lived there.

TAB-FULL:v10p325/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the phrase as if they had never been there at all.

TAB-FULL:v10p325/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p325/r6.claim: Shuʿayb’s followers were not the losers; God refuted the deniers’ warning in 7:90 by making the deniers the ones destroyed when punishment came.

TABATABAI:7:90-92/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r2.claim: Mentioning this threat here prepares for the later reversal: those who called Shu'ayb's followers losers are followed by the declaration that the deniers themselves were the losers.
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r2.anchor: ويكون إفراد هذا بالذكر ها هنا من بين سائر أقوالهم ليكون كالتوطئة والتمهيد لما سيأتي

TABATABAI:7:90-92/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r5.claim: The threat may also be taken as directed at following Shu'ayb's religious message; on either reading it anticipates the next verse's reversal of who truly loses.
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r5.anchor: وعلى أي الوجهين كان فالآية كالتوطئة والتمهيد للآية الآتية

TABATABAI:7:90-92/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r7.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r7.claim: Al-Raghib defines living in a place as staying there a long time, finding it sufficient and needing no other place.
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r7.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات وغني في مكان كذا إذا طال مقامه فيه مستغنيا به عن غيره بغنى

TABATABAI:7:90-92/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r8.claim: Ka'an is the shortened form of ka'anna, lightened because it introduces a verbal clause.
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r8.anchor: و { كأن } مخفف كأن خفف لدخوله الجملة الفعلية

TABATABAI:7:90-92/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r9.claim: The simile depicts the deniers as people who had not lived long in their land: transient residents leave easily, while a rooted population is attached to kin, homes, estates, and possessions and finds departure almost impossible.
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r9.anchor: فيه تشبيه حال المكذبين من قومه بمن لم يطيلوا الإقامة في أرضهم فإن أمثال هؤلاء يسهل زوالهم لعدم تعلقهم بها

TABATABAI:7:90-92/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r10.claim: Though deeply established in their land, Shu'ayb's people abandoned it and all they owned in an instant when the quake left them crouched dead in their homes; their confidence that he and his followers would be driven out was reversed.
TABATABAI:7:90-92/r10.anchor: وقد ترك هؤلاء وهم أمة عريقة في الأرض دارهم وما فيها

TABATABAI:7:91-93/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:91-93/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:91-93/r1.claim: The sequence overturns the chiefs' boast: the punishment first leaves its victims implicit, then 7:92 names the deniers as those destroyed and truly made losers, contrary to their claim about Shu'ayb's followers.
TABATABAI:7:91-93/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر نزول العذاب وأبهم الذين أخذتهم الرجفة فقال { فأخذتهم الرجفة } ولم يقل فأخذت الذين كفروا الرجفة

TABRISI:7:90-93/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:90-93/r4.claim: The first “those who denied Shuayb” is nominative as subject, with “as though they had never lived there” as its predicate; repeating the phrase instead of using a pronoun intensifies the charge.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r4.anchor: الذين كذبوا سيما الأول في موضع رفع بالابتداء وخبره كأن لم يغنوا فيها وإنما أعيد مرة ثانية من غير كناية

TABRISI:7:90-93/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:90-93/r5.claim: Hum is a separating pronoun that emphasizes the meaning; it is needed for emphasis even though a pronoun is not ordinarily modified, and the definite predicate still functions as a predicate.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r5.anchor: وهم في قوله هم الخاسرين فصل وإنما دخل الفصل مع أن المضمر لا يوصف لأنه يحتاج فيه إلى التوكيد

TABRISI:7:90-93/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:90-93/r15.claim: The destruction made it seem that they had never existed there.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r15.anchor: أي كأنهم لم يقيموا بها قط لأن المهلك يصير كأن لم يكن

TABRISI:7:90-93/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r16.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:7:90-93/r16.claim: Qatada glosses it as though they had not lived there in ease and self-sufficiency.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r16.anchor: وقيل: كأن لم يغنوا فيها كأن لم يعيشوا فيها مستغنين عن قتادة

TABRISI:7:90-93/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:7:90-93/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses it as though they had not inhabited the place.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r17.anchor: وقيل: كأن لم يعمروا فيها عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:7:90-93/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:90-93/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:90-93/r18.claim: The repeated phrase “those who denied Shuayb” intensifies the condemnation and underscores that they, rather than the believers, were the losers.
TABRISI:7:90-93/r18.anchor: مر معناه بين سبحانه أنهم الخاسرون دون من آمن به

THALABI:v4p263/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p263/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p263/r3.claim: The phrase means they had never lived, stayed, settled, or enjoyed life there; غنى بالمكان means remain, and مغاني are dwellings, singular مغنى.
THALABI:v4p263/r3.anchor: أي لم يعيشوا ولم ينزلوا ولم يقيموا ولم ينعموا، وأصله من قولهم غنية بالمكان إذا أقمت به

THALABI:v4p263/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p263/r4.speaker: لبيد
THALABI:v4p263/r4.claim: Labid's line uses غنيت for having lived somewhere, evidence for the phrase's sense.
THALABI:v4p263/r4.anchor:
قال لبيد:
وغنيت ستا قبل مجرى داهس … لو كان للنفس اللجوج خلود

THALABI:v4p263/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p263/r5.speaker: حاتم
THALABI:v4p263/r5.claim: Hatim's line uses غنينا for dwelling in two conditions, supporting the sense of living in a place.
THALABI:v4p263/r5.anchor:
وقال حاتم:
غنينا زمانا للتصعلك والغنى … فكلا سقانا بكأسيهما الدهر

THALABI:v4p263/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p263/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p263/r6.claim: The people who truly lost were those who denied Shuaib, not the believers as they had claimed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r1.speaker: أبو علي الجرجاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r1.claim: Abu Ali al-Jurjani says this phrase supplies the referent of the concealed pronouns in the preceding verse, as in 11:67–68 and 5:71.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r1.anchor: مثل قوله: {عموا وصموا كثير منهم} [المائدة: 71]، قاله أبو علي الجرجاني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r2.claim: غني القوم في دارهم can mean that people stayed a long time in their home; مغاني are dwellings and مغنى is singular.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r2.anchor: يقال: غني (¬5) القوم في دارهم: إذا طال مقامهم فيها، والمغاني: المنازل التي كان بها أهلوها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r3.claim: The exegetes gloss the phrase as though the people had never lived or settled there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬3): (كأن لم يقيموا فيها ولم ينزلوا فيها).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives an alternative sense: they seemed never to have lived there in comfort, taking يغنوا from wealth or sufficiency; a poem uses غنينا to mean we lived.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: (ويكون {كأن لم يغنوا فيها}: كأن لم يعيشوا فيها مستغنين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari agrees with the sense of never having lived in prosperity, deriving the verb from being free of need rather than dwelling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r5.anchor: ووافقه ابن الأنباري على هذا المعنى، فقال في قوله: {كأن لم يغنوا فيها}:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r6.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as though they had never enjoyed blessings there, supporting the prosperity reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r6.anchor: يؤكد هذا المعنى ما روي عن قتادة أنه قال في هذه الآية: (كأن لم ينعموا فيها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r7.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r7.claim: The cited verse about the space between al-Hajun and al-Safa portrays their condition as if no one had ever lived in those dwellings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r7.anchor:
كما قال الشاعر:
كأن لم يكن بين الحجون إلى الصفا ... أنيس ولم يسمر بمكة سامر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r8.claim: The verse describes the deniers' terrible end: punishment and loss left them as though they had never enjoyed worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p237/r8.anchor: إبانة عن سوء حال المكذب نبيا من أنبياء الله في أنه بمنزلة من لم يستمتع بالدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p240/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p240/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p240/r1.claim: The repeated clause begins a new, disconnected nominal sentence consisting of subject and predicate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p240/r1.anchor: هذا ابتداء منقطع من الفصل الأول، جملة من المبتدأ والخبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p240/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p240/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p240/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the repetition intensifies blame and magnifies their deserved punishment, as Arabs repeat accusations for emphasis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p240/r2.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (ووقع التكرير لتعظيم الذم لهم و (¬2) تفظيع ما يستحقون من الجزاء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:92-93/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:92-93/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:92-93/r1.claim: It means they had not lived or settled there.

ELMALILI:7:92/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:92/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:92/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the deniers as seeming never to have enjoyed themselves in that land.
ELMALILI:7:92/r1.anchor: Şuayb’ı tekzib edenler sandı ki bu diyarda safâ sürmemişlerdi

ELMALILI:7:92/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:92/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:92/r2.claim: The deniers include those who threatened to expel Shuaib and the believers from their town.
ELMALILI:7:92/r2.anchor: Şuayb’ı tekzib edenler; “onu ve maiyyetindeki mü’minleri karyemizden çıkarırız” diye

ELMALILI:7:92/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:92/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:92/r3.claim: They also said that whoever followed Shuaib would certainly be among the losers.

ELMALILI:7:92/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:92/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:92/r4.claim: The losers were the deniers themselves, not Shuaib or his followers.
ELMALILI:7:92/r4.anchor: ancak kendileri hâsirîn oldular. Şuayb ve ona tâbi‘olanlar değil.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r1.claim: Madyan’s unbelieving, oppressive elite threatened Shuʿayb’s people, but suffered their deserved catastrophe and vanished as if no one had lived there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r1.anchor: asıl kendileri hak ettikleri büyük felâkete uğramışlar; bu dünyada öyle bir topluluk yaşamamış gibi yok olup gitmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r2.claim: Because Shuʿayb had done everything to rescue them from error and avert this fate, there was no reason to pity them afterward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r2.anchor: Şuayb, daha önce onları dalâletten kurtarmak ve böyle bir âkıbete mâruz kalmalarını önlemek için elinden gelen her şeyi yaptığından

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r3.claim: The preceding accounts of five prophets are concise lessons about their calls, people's responses, and the disasters suffered by oppressors, rather than history for its own sake.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r3.anchor: beş peygamberin kendi toplumlarıyla ilişkileri, davetlerinin mahiyeti, bu davet karşısında inanan ve inanmayanların tutumları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r4.claim: The ensuing verses present communities' calamities and hardships as having the purpose of reforming people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:90/r4.anchor: Müteakip âyetlerde ise bütün bu toplumların uğradığı felâketlerin, zorlukların insanları ıslah etmeye yönelik amaçlar taşıdığı bildirilmektedir

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#3/r1.claim: The phrase means they had not lived there; ghaniy bimaḍin means to dwell in a place.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#3/r1.anchor: {كأن لم يغنوا فيها} أي لم يقيموا فيها. يقال: غنينا بمكان كذا: أقمنا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p170#3/r2.claim: Dwellings are called maghānī, singular maghnā.

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r1.claim: One parse makes the first relative a subject and the comparison clause its predicate; al-Zamakhshari says this fronting restricts destruction to deniers of Shuayb, since his followers were saved.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وفي هذا الابتداء معنى الاختصاص كأنه قيل: الذين كذبوا شعيبا هم المخصوصون

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r2.claim: The author equates the claimed اختصاص with the usul notion of restriction, while noting disagreement about its force in noun-first and predicate-first formulations.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r2.anchor: قلت: قوله " يفيد الاختصاص " هو معنى قول الأصوليين: " يفيد الحصر " على خلاف بينهم في ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r3.claim: A second parse makes the second relative and its clause the predicate of the first; كأن لم يغنوا is parenthetical or circumstantial to كذبوا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r3.anchor: الثاني: أن الخبر هو نفس الموصول الثاني وخبره

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r4.claim: A third parse treats the second relative as a second predicate, with the comparison clause serving as the first predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r4.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون الموصول الثاني خبرا بعد خبر عن الموصول الأول، والخبر الأول الجملة التشبيهية كما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r5.claim: A fourth parse makes the relative بدل of الذين كفروا من قومه in 7:90, within the preceding report of what the leaders said.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r5.anchor:
الرابع: أن يكون الموصول بدلا من قوله قبل
الذين كفروا من قومه

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa and the Shaykh describe the relative as an adjective of الذين كفروا من قومه; the author refines this to الملأ as the actual antecedent.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r6.anchor: عبارة أبي البقاء، وتابعه الشيخ عليها

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r7.claim: The author prefers parsing the relative as بدل from الملأ or an adjective of الملأ; on either option, the comparison clause is circumstantial to كذبوا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r7.anchor: والأحسن أن يقال: بدل من الملأ أو نعت له، لأنه هو المحدث عنه

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r8.claim: The second relative can serve as first or second predicate; it can also be بدل of the subject of يغنوا, an object under implied أعني, or a new subject.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r8.anchor: وأما الموصول الثاني فقد تقدم أنه يجوز أن يكون خبرا باعتبارين: أعني كونه أول أو ثانيا

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r9.claim: The clearest parse makes the second relative a new subject with كانوا هم الخاسرين as its predicate, so each sentence stands independently.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r9.anchor: وهذا هو الظاهر لتكون كل جملة مستقلة بنفسها

SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says beginning the second sentence with the relative restricts great loss to Shuayb's deniers, excluding his followers.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92/r10.anchor: ذكر الزمخشري أيضا أن الابتداء يفيد الاختصاص قال: " أي هم المخصوصون بالخسران العظيم

SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r1.claim: غني بالمكان means to reside there for a long time; some narrow it to living there in comfort and prosperity.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r1.anchor: غني بالمكان يغنى فيه أي: أقام دهرا طويلا

SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r2.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r2.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur's line ولقد غنوا فيها بأنعم عيشة supports the narrower sense of dwelling in ease and prosperity.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r2.anchor:
قال الأسود بن يعفر:
2249 ولقد غنوا فيها بأنعم عيشة

SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives the phrase from wealth, opposite poverty: to be غني in a place is to stay there long while needing nothing from elsewhere.
SAMIN-DURR:7:92#2/r3.anchor: قاله الزجاج فقال: " وغني في مكان كذا: إذا طال مقامه فيه مستغنيا به عن غيره "

ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r6.claim: The phrase means as if they had not dwelt there; al-Asma'i says المغاني are places of residence and غنينا بمكان means we settled there.
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r6.anchor: المغاني المنازل التي نزلوا بها، يقال غنينا بمكان كذا وكذا، أي نزلنا به.

ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r7.speaker: الشاعر حاتم طي
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r7.claim: The phrase may also evoke having lived there in ease and prosperity; Hatim al-Ta'i's poem uses غنينا alongside التصعلك and الغنى, and Arabs call a poor person a ṣuʿluk.
ZAJJAJ:v2p357/r7.anchor: قال حاتم طي: غنينا زمانا بالتصعلك والغنى.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains lam yaghnaw as they did not dwell there; another version says it was as if they had never existed, with a gloss specifying this world at the time of punishment.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r1.anchor: قال: لم يعمروا فيها. قال فيه مهلهل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r2.claim: The cited poems of Muhalhil and Labid witness the sense of dwelling or living in a place; Labid's line is the common poetic evidence across the cited versions.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p483/r2.anchor: وقال فيه لبيد: وغنيتُ سبتاً قبل مجرى داحسٍ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.claim: God's law applies equally to every nation: after a messenger comes, a people must accept reform or face destruction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.anchor: When God sends a messenger to a nation, it is faced with either of the two options: to accept reformation or be put to death.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.claim: Arabs knew these nations' stories through vague traditions, especially lacking their moral lessons; the Qur’an restores that history and tells Quraysh to learn that these are their own warning stories.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p57/.anchor: Their moral aspect, in particular, was totally ambiguous. The Qur’ ān has lifted the veil from this ambiguity and revived their history.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.claim: The warning to Quraysh begins with accounts of peoples known across Arabia's north, south, and northwest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.anchor: those nations are taken up which became famous while inhabiting the north, the south and the north west of Arabia.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.claim: The nations in these accounts were destroyed for denying their messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.anchor: All of them were destroyed because they denied their respective messengers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.claim: The accounts follow historical order, so Noah's nation is treated first.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p60/.anchor: The sequence adopted is historical. For this reason, the nation of Noah (sws) is taken up the first.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.claim: The disbelievers’ erasure from their settlement reverses their threat to expel Shuʿayb and his followers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.anchor: While referring to this threat, it is said that they themselves were wiped out from their settlement as if they never existed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.claim: The second sentence reverses the disbelievers’ warning that Shuʿayb’s followers would incur a great loss: the rejectors themselves lost.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p81/.anchor: those who rejected Shu‘ayb (sws) were the ones who had incurred a loss.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p233#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p233#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p233#3/r1.claim: Qatāda explains the phrase as if they had never lived there or enjoyed its blessings.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p233#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ كأن لم يغنوا فيها ﴾ قال كأن لم يعيشوا فيها كأن لم ينعموا فيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r1.claim: The phrase pictures them as having never lived in their settled, comfortable homes, intensifying the report of their destruction and inviting reflection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r1.anchor: أي كأن لم يقيموا ناعمي البال رخيي العيش في دارهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r2.claim: The image of a place emptied of its former inhabitants recalls 10:24 and a poem imagining Makkah without its familiar residents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r2.anchor: كقوله تعالى: فجعلناها حصيدا كأن لم تغن بالأمس وكقول الشاعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says living in a place with this verb denotes residence joined with luxury and ease, a sense he infers from Arabic poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وغنيت بالمكان إنما يقال في الإقامة التي هي مقترنة بتنعم وعيش رخي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as if they had not built or inhabited for long.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كان لم يعمروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r5.claim: Qatāda explains the phrase as if they had never enjoyed well-being.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r6.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r6.claim: Qatāda, Ibn Zayd, and Muqātil understand it as if they had never existed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r6.anchor: وقال أيضا قتادة وابن زيد ومقاتل: كأن لم يكونوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses the phrase as if they had never alighted there.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses it as if they had not stayed there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: كأن لم يقيموا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r9.claim: He parses the first الذين clause as a subject whose predicate is the following simile clause.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the initial construction as restrictive: those who denied Shuʿayb alone were annihilated, while his followers were saved.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r10.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وفي هذا الابتداء معنى الاختصاص كأنه قيل الذين كذبوا شعيبا المخصوصون بأن أهلكوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r11.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows the second clause to be the predicate, with the simile serving as a circumstantial clause attached to the pronoun in كذبوا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r11.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون الخبر الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين وكأن لم يغنوا حال من الضمير في كذبوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r12.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r12.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows the clause to modify or replace قومه in the preceding speech, making the simile circumstantial.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r12.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون الذين كذبوا صفة لقول الذين كفروا من قومه وأن يكون بدلا منه وعلى هذين الوجهين يكون كأن حالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r13.claim: He rejects those attached parses as strained and prefers treating the clauses as syntactically independent of what precedes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r13.anchor: وهذه أوجه متكلفة والظاهر أنها جمل مستقلة لا تعلق بما قبلها من جهة الإعراب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r14.claim: He parses the second الذين clause as an independent subject and predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r14.anchor: الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين هذا أيضا مبتدأ وخبره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the second opening as restrictive too: the deniers alone incur immense loss, whereas Shuʿayb's followers gain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r15.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وفيه معنى الاختصاص أي هم المخصوصون بالخسران العظيم دون اتباعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the fresh opening and repetition emphatically rebut the chiefs' claim, expose their poor judgment, ridicule their advice, and magnify their fate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r16.anchor: وفي هذا الاستئناف لهذا الابتداء وهذا التكرير مبالغة في رد مقالة الملأ لأشياعهم وتسفيه لرأيهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r17.claim: The two clauses reverse the chiefs' threats: God reports their expulsion through destruction and assigns loss to them rather than Shuʿayb's followers, answering 7:88.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r17.anchor: وهاتان الجملتان منبئتان عن ما فعل الله بهم في مقالتهم قالوا لنخرجنك يا شعيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r18.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r18.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows الذين here to replace the pronoun in يغنوا or to be an understood accusative of specification; the author prefers the independent subject analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p116#2/r18.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء في إعراب الذين هنا أن يكون بدلا من الضمير في يغنوا أو منصوبا بإضمار أعني والابتداء الذي ذكرناه أقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r1.claim: The resumption explains the evil consequence of the people’s threat to expel Shuʿayb and the believers in 7:88.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r1.anchor: استئناف لبيان ابتلائهم بشؤم قولهم : ( لنخرجنك ياشعيب والذين آمنوا معك من قريتنا )

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r2.claim: The relative clause is subject; its predicate says they seemed never to have dwelt in their homes.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r2.anchor: والموصول مبتدأ خبره قوله تعالى : كأن لم يغنوا فيها أي لم يقيموا في دارهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r3.claim: Qatāda explains the expression as if they had not lived there in comfortable self-sufficiency.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة : المعنى كأن لم يعيشوا فيها مستغنين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r4.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r4.claim: Many say ghanā bi-l-makān means to remain there a long time; some restrict it to living there in prosperity.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r4.anchor: وذكر غير واحد أنه يقال : غنى بالمكان يغني غنى وغنيانا إذا أقام به دهرا طويلا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī and others connect the root with wealth rather than residence, citing Ḥātim’s poem about experiencing both poverty and wealth; this fits Qatāda’s gloss.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري كغيره : إنه من الغنى ضد الفقر كما في قول حاتم : غنينا زمانا بالتصعلك والغنى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r6.claim: Some paraphrase the outcome as their being completely annihilated.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r6.anchor: وقول بعضهم في بيان الآية : إنهم استؤصلوا بالمرة بيان لحاصل المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r7.claim: Making the predicate depend on the relative clause hints that denial caused their lasting destruction and implies the believers’ lasting escape; the contrast with earlier mention of both groups can signal exclusivity.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r7.anchor: وفي بناء الخبر على الموصول إيماء إلى أن علة الحكم هي الصلة فكأنه قيل : الذين كذبوا شعيبا هلكوا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r8.claim: They were punished for threatening expulsion and became the ones expelled from the town without return, while Shuʿayb and his followers did not.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p6#2/r8.anchor: ويرجع حاصل المعنى بالآخرة إلى أنهم عوقبوا بتوعدهم السابق بالإخراج وصاروا هم المخرجين من القرية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r1.claim: The second resumption explains the punishment for their final claim: the deniers, not Shuʿayb’s followers, lost both worldly life and religion, reversing their warning in 7:90; this implies their rescue as 11:94 states explicitly.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r1.anchor: استئناف آخر لبيان ابتلائهم بعقوبة قولهم الأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r2.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r2.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the repeated resumption and relative clause intensify the refutation of the chiefs’ advice, ridicule it, and magnify what happened to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r2.anchor: وفي الكشاف أن في هذا الاستئناف وتكرير الموصول والصلة مبالغة في رد مقالة الملأ لأشياعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds it difficult to derive all those rhetorical effects from this verse alone; the combined two resumptions more clearly suggest them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r3.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن في استفادة ذلك كله من نفس هذه الآية خفاء والظاهر أن مجموع الاستئنافين مؤذن به

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r4.claim: Al-Ṭībī explains that the first resumption answers what became of them after the earthquake: they were annihilated as though they had never lived there.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r4.anchor: وبين الطيبي ذلك بأنه تعالى لما رتب العقاب بأخذ الرجفة وتركهم هامدين لا حراك بهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r5.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r5.claim: Al-Ṭībī says the second resumption answers whether destruction extended beyond them: it specifies that ruin was theirs alone, and the repeated clause makes the report emphatic and exclusive.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r5.anchor: ثم سأل أخصص الدمار بهم أم تعدى إلى غيرهم فقيل : ( الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين )

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r6.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r6.claim: Al-Ṭībī adds that the second clause makes their own warning turn against them: what they called advice became disgrace, and those they called losers were not the losers.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r6.anchor: وجاء تسفيه الرأي من الرد عليهم بعين ما تلفظوا به في نصح قومهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r7.claim: Al-Ṭībī reads the definite generic “losers” as magnifying the loss; the image of seeming never to have lived and the whole statement magnify the calamity.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r7.anchor: ويستفاد عظم الخسران من تعريف الخبر بلام الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r8.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r8.claim: Some say Arabs use such unconnected resumptions habitually for blame and rebuke, as in “your brother who plundered our property; your brother who violated our protection.”
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r8.anchor: وقد ذكر غير واحد أن هذا الاستئناف من غير عطف جار على عادة العرب في مثل هذا المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r9.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r9.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ offers alternatives: the second relative clause may appose the pronoun in “they dwelt,” be an omitted “I mean” in the accusative, or serve as predicate while the first clause is circumstantial; he also allows adjectival or appositional analyses.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p7/r9.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون الموصول الثاني بدلا من الضمير في ( يغنوا ) وأن يكون في محل نصب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r1.claim: يغنوا means they did not stay or settle there; مغاني means dwellings, singular مغنى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r2.claim: An alternative says the phrase means it was as though they had never enjoyed life there.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r3.claim: The ones who truly lost were those who rejected Shuayb, not the believers as the chiefs claimed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p259/r3.anchor: {الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين} لا المؤمنين كما زعموا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r1.claim: The first relative clause is a subject whose predicate is “as though they had never lived there”; maghnā means a dwelling place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r1.anchor: مبتدأ خبره { كأن لم يغنوا فيها }

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r2.claim: They were uprooted as if they had never lived there; maghnā means a dwelling place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r2.anchor: أي استؤصلوا كأن لم يقيموا بها والمغنى المنزل

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r3.claim: The deniers lost in religion and worldly life; those who believed and followed Shuʿayb, despite the deniers’ claim, gained in both abodes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r3.anchor: دينا ودنيا لا الذين صدقوه واتبعوه كما زعموا

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r4.claim: Repeating the relative clause and using two independent nominal sentences emphasizes this reversal.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:92/r4.anchor: كرر الموصول واستأنف بالجملتين وأتى بهما اسميتين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r7.claim: They seemed never to have lived or stayed there; their former abode and life of leisure, celebration, and self-sufficiency had vanished.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r7.anchor: أي ينزلوا ويقيموا , وبطل مقامهم لاهين بالأفراح والغناء والاستغناء من المغاني وهي المنازل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r8.claim: Repeating that those who rejected Shuayb were the losers underscores their especially shameful rejection, which caused their loss of bodies and souls, while his followers suffered none.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p71/r8.anchor: ولما كان تكذيب الصادقين لا سيما الرسل في غاية الشناعة , كرره إشارة إلى ذلك وإعلاما بأنه سبب لهم أعظم من هلاك الشباح

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1524/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1524/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1524/r1.claim: Qatāda explains the phrase as saying that they had not lived or enjoyed prosperity there.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1524/r1.anchor: عن قتادة كان لم يغنوا فيها كان لم يعيشوا فيها ، كان لم ينعموا فيها

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1524/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1524/r2.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1524/r2.claim: Abū Mālik says the phrase means it was as though they had never been there.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1524/r2.anchor: عن أبي مالك قال : كان لم يغنوا فيها كان لم يكونوا فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r6.claim: “Those who denied Shuʿayb” begins a new independent sentence; its relative wording hints that their destruction and extinction were punishment for denial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r6.anchor: مستأنفة ابتدائية ، والتعريف بالموصولية للإيماء إلى وجه بناء الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r7.claim: Ghanā bi-l-makān means to reside there; hence maghnā names a people's dwelling place.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the Arabic poetry he surveyed uses ghanā for residence accompanied by comfortable living, perhaps from istighnā (being self-sufficient).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r8.anchor: ابن عطية : ( الذي استقريت من أشعار العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r9.claim: The comparison concerns the annihilation of their traces, not merely their death, which is true of every dead person; 10:24 gives a similar image.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r9.anchor: وهذا إنما يعنى به انمحاء آثارهم كما قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r10.claim: The total erasure suggests that earthquake and lightning burned their bodies, buried them, and overturned their dwellings beneath the earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r10.anchor: وهو يرجح أن يكون أصابهم زلزال مع الصواعق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r11.claim: Fronting “those who denied Shuʿayb” strengthens the assertion if kāna is verbal; if it is a copula, the nominal sentence's stability supplies the emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p13/r11.anchor: إذا اعتبرت { كانوا } فعلا ، واعتبر المسند فعليا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p14/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p14/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p14/r1.claim: Repeating “those who denied Shuʿayb” enumerates and awakens the Arab polytheist audience, indirectly warning them to avoid the fate of earlier idolaters and deniers, as stated explicitly in 47:10.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p14/r1.anchor: والتكرير لقوله : { الذين كذبوا شعيبا } للتعديد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p14/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p14/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p14/r2.claim: The separating pronoun gives an additional restriction: the deniers, unlike Shuʿayb's followers, were the losers, exposing the chiefs' foolish claim that following him would mean loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p14/r2.anchor: دون الذين اتبعوا شعيبا ، وذلك لإظهار سفه قول الملإ للعامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r2.claim: The phrase stresses how completely destruction and punishment overtook them and presents them as a lesson to others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r2.anchor: لفظ فيه للإخبار عن قوة هلاكهم ونزول النقمة بهم والتنبيه على العبرة بهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r3.claim: Here yaghnu means to reside and live in a place; a cited line about the route between al-Ḥajūn and al-Ṣafā illustrates the sense.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r4.claim: The author’s survey of Arabic poetry suggests that ghani in a place denotes residence joined with comfort and a pleasant life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r4.anchor: غنيت في المكان إنما يقال في الإقامة التي هي مقترنة بتنعم وعيش مرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r5.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r5.claim: The line “وقد نغنى بها” is cited as evidence for the place-based sense of living amid comfortable circumstances.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r5.anchor: قول الشاعر: [الوافر] وقد نغنى بها ونرى عصورا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r6.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r6.claim: A line about neighbors who “lived” there while maintaining a pact and connection is another example of the term’s place-based usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r6.anchor: قول الآخر: [الرمل] ولقد يغنى بها جيرانك المس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r7.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r7.claim: The phrase “المغانيا” in a love poem is cited among poetic examples of this usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r7.anchor: ومنه قول الآخر: [الطويل] ألا حي من أجل الحبيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r8.speaker: مهلهل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r8.claim: Muhalhil’s line about the family’s home in Tihama provides another example of ghani used with a place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r8.anchor: ومنه قول مهلهل: [الخفيف] غنيت دارنا تهامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r9.claim: The author suggests the word may derive from istighnāʾ, “being independent or self-sufficient.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r9.anchor: ويشبه أن تكون اللفظة من الاستغناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r10.claim: “As though they had not lived there yesterday” depicts them as if they had never been flourishing, thriving, and established.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p430/r10.anchor: لأن المراد كأن لم تكن ناعمة نضرة مستقلة،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Akhfash gloss the phrase as if they had not lived in their homes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r1.anchor: أحدها كأن لم يعيشوا في دارهم قاله ابن عباس والأخفش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r2.speaker: حاتم طيئ
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r2.claim: A line by Hatim al-Ta'i uses ghaniyna for living; the cited poem supports this sense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r2.anchor: قال حاتم طيئ غنينا زمانا بالتصعلك والغنى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ghaniyna means they lived; taṣaʿluk means poverty, and Arabs call a poor person a ṣuʿlūk.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج منى غنينا عشنا والتصعلك الفقر والعرب تقول للفقير الصعلوك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r4.claim: Qatada explains the phrase as if they had not enjoyed life there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r4.anchor: والثاني كأن لم يتنعموا فيها قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r5.speaker: ابن زيد ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd and Muqatil explain it as if they had never been there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r5.anchor: والثالث كأن لم يكونوا فيها قاله ابن زيد ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj's fourth explanation is as if they had never settled there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r6.anchor: والرابع كأن لم ينزلوا فيها قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r7.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r7.claim: Al-Asma'i says maghānī are dwellings, and ghaniyna in a place means they settled there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r7.anchor: قال الأصمعي المغاني المنازل يقال غنينا بمكان كذا أي نزلنا بمكان كذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the phrase means they did not remain there; ghaniyna in a place means they resided there.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r8.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة كأن لم يقيموا فيها ومعنى غنينا بمكان كذا أقمنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r9.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the repeated description of those who denied Shuayb intensifies their condemnation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p232/r9.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري وإنما كرر قوله ﴿ الذين كذبوا شعيبا ﴾ للمبالغة في ذمهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r4.claim: After punishment, it was as if they had never lived in the homes from which they had meant to drive the Messenger and his followers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r4.anchor: أي: كأنهم لما أصابتهم النقمة لم يقيموا بديارهم التي أرادوا إجلاء الرسول وصحبه منها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r5.claim: The conclusion reverses their boast that Shuʿayb's followers would be the losers: the deniers themselves were the losers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p448#2/r5.anchor: ثم قال مقابلا لقيلهم: {الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين}

JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r1.claim: Khusr is the loss of one’s capital; the related verb is used for incurring loss.
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r1.anchor: الخسر: إذهاب رأس المال، يقال: خسر خسرانا.

JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r3.claim: Maghānī are dwellings; ghaniya bi-l-makān means to reside there, as if that place made one independent of others, from the root meaning wealth or sufficiency.
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r3.anchor: والمغاني: المنازل، وغني بالمكان يغني غناء: إذا قام به كأنه استغنى بذلك المكان عن غيره،

JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r4.claim: In answer to Nafiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas glosses ‘as though they had not lived there’ as ‘as though they had not inhabited it.’
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r4.anchor: وسأل نافع بن الأزرق ابن عباس عن قوله: كأن لم يغنوا فيها؟ قال: كأن لم يعمروا،

JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r5.speaker: مهلهل
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r5.claim: Muhalhil’s verse uses ghaniya of a dwelling in Tihama that had long been inhabited, illustrating the word’s dwelling sense.
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r5.anchor: قال مهلهل: غنيت دارنا تهامة في الده

JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r6.speaker: لبيد
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r6.claim: Labid’s verse likewise uses ghaniya to mean dwelling or remaining in a place.
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r6.anchor: وقال لبيد: وغنيت سبتا قبل مجرى داحس

JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r7.claim: The source also records ghaniya in the sense ‘became beautiful.’
JISHUMI:v4p2638#2/r7.anchor: ويقال للشيء تغنى كأن لم يغن بالأمس إن كان لم يكن قيما بمكان، ويقال: غنيت: جملت.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r5.claim: الذين كذبوا شعيبا is a subject whose predicate is كأن لم يغنوا فيها; the repeated clause likewise has كانوا هم الخاسرين as its predicate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r5.anchor: مبتدأ خبره { كأن لم يغنوا فيها } وكذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r6.claim: The opening gives exclusive focus: Shuʿayb’s deniers alone were annihilated as if they had never lived there, while his followers were saved; they alone suffered the great loss.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r7.claim: The resumptive opening and repetition emphatically refute the chiefs’ claim, disparage their judgment, mock their advice, and magnify their people’s fate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p124#2/r7.anchor: مبالغة في رد مقالة الملإ لأشياعهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses the phrase as though they had never stayed there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r1.anchor: أحدها : كأنك لم يقيموا فيها , قاله ابن قتيبة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r2.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses the phrase as though they had never lived there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r2.anchor: والثاني : كأن لم يعيشوا فيها , قاله الأخفش .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r3.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r3.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as though they had never enjoyed life there.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r3.anchor: والثالث : كأن لم ينعموا فيها , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as though they had never inhabited it for a long time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r4.anchor: والرابع : كأن لم يعمروا فيها , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r5.claim: Their loss is explained as loss through unbelief or destruction; the latter gloss is attributed to Ibn Abbas.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p241/r5.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : بالكفر . والثاني : بالهلاك , قاله ابن عباس .

MUQATIL:7:90-93/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r4.claim: It was as though they had never lived there at all.
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r4.anchor: يعنى كأن لم يكونوا فيها قط

MUQATIL:7:90-93/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r5.claim: Those who denied Shuʿayb were the losers.
MUQATIL:7:90-93/r5.anchor: الذين كذبوا شعيبا كانوا هم الخاسرين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r1.claim: The first «those who denied Shuʿayb» is the subject whose predicate is «as though they had never lived there»; yaghnu means residing.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ الذين كذبوا شعيبا ﴾ مبتدأ خبره ﴿ كأن لم يغنوا فيها ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r2.claim: «Lam yaghnu» means they had not remained or lived in the land.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r2.anchor: لم يقيموا فيها غنى بالمكان أقام

NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r3.claim: The clause restricts the title of losers to Shuʿayb’s deniers: they were destroyed as though never there, while his followers were saved and were the real winners.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r3.anchor: وفى هذا الابتداء معنى الاختصاص كأنه قي الذين كذبوا شعيبا المخصوصون

NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r4.claim: Repeating «those who denied Shuʿayb» magnifies their denial and what befell them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p25#3/r4.anchor: مبالغة واستعظام لتكذيهم ولما جرى عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r5.speaker: الجرجاني
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r5.claim: Al-Jurjani says the phrase begins a new sentence: those who denied Shuayb became as though they had always been dead.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r5.anchor: قال الجرجاني: قيل هذا كلام مستأنف أي الذين كذبوا شعيبا صاروا كأنهم لم يزالوا موتى.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r6.claim: Yaghnu means dwell or remain; ghaniya bi-l-makan means reside, and maghna means home, plural maghani.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r6.anchor: يقال: غنيت بالمكان إذا أقمت به. وغني القوم في دارهم أي طال مقامهم فيها.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r7.speaker: لبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r7.claim: Labid uses ghanit for dwelling somewhere six years before the race of Dahis.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r7.anchor: قال لبيد: وغنيت ستا قبل مجرى داحس لو كان للنفس اللجوج خلود

QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r8.speaker: حاتم طي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r8.claim: Hatim al-Ta'i uses ghanina for living through poverty and wealth; fortune did not make them arrogant or poverty disgrace them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:90-92/r8.anchor: وقال حاتم طي: غنينا زمانا بالتصعلك والغنى كما الدهر في أيامه العسر واليسر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:92-93/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:92-93/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:92-93/r1.claim: The repeated statement that Shuayb's deniers were losers begins a new address and intensifies blame; those who called Shuayb's followers losers are the true losers.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:92-93/r1.anchor: ابتداء خطاب، وهو مبالغة في الذم والتوبيخ وإعادة لتعظيم الأمر وتفخيمه.

BURSEVI:v3p154/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p154/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p154/r1.claim: This clause resumes the account to explain the consequence of their threat to expel Shuayb and the believers.
BURSEVI:v3p154/r1.anchor: استئناف لبيان ابتلائهم بشؤم قولهم فيما سبق

BURSEVI:v3p154/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p154/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p154/r2.claim: They were eradicated as if never resident there; punishment inverted their threat, leaving them expelled forever. مغنى means dwelling, and غنينا بمكان means residing there.
BURSEVI:v3p154/r2.anchor: أي : استأصلوا بالمرة وصاروا كأنهم لم يقيموا بقريتهم أصلا

BURSEVI:v3p154/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p154/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p154/r3.claim: Deniers and the arrogant may prevail briefly, but their fame and traces disappear, while truth's followers ultimately prevail.
BURSEVI:v3p154/r3.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن المكذبين والمتكبرين وإن كانت لهم غلبة في وقتهم ولكن تنقضي أيامهم بسرعة

BURSEVI:v3p154/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p154/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p154/r4.claim: The Masnavi verses recall deniers publicly and urge choosing the victorious side rather than allying with the defeated.
BURSEVI:v3p154/r4.anchor: يك مناره در ثناى منكران كودرين عالم كه تاباشد عيان

BURSEVI:v3p154#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p154#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p154#2/r1.claim: A second resumption says they were punished for their final statement and lost worldly and religious life, unlike Shuayb's followers; emphasis replaces an explicit rescue statement, as in 11:58.
BURSEVI:v3p154#2/r1.anchor: استئناف آخر لبيان ابتلائهم بعقوبة قولهم الأخير

RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r6.claim: One explanation says ghani means that people stayed a long time in their home; maghna refers to a dwelling.
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r6.anchor: يقال غني القوم في دارهم إذا طال مقامهم فيها

RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r7.speaker: الشاعر
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r7.claim: An unnamed poet's line about their having lived amid the best life witnesses the sense 'they dwelled there'.
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r7.anchor: قال الشاعر : ولقد غنوا فيها بأنعم عيشة … في ظل ملك ثابت الأوتاد

RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r8.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains it as 'as if they had not lived there in comfort'; ghaniya means becoming self-sufficient, from richness opposed to poverty.
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج : كأن لم يغنوا فيها ، كأن لم يعيشوا فيها مستغنين

RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r9.claim: On either interpretation, God likens the deniers to people who had never been in those dwellings, as a poet's lines illustrate.
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r9.anchor: كأن لم يكن بين الحجون إلى الصفا … أنيس ولم يسمر بمكة سامر

RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r10.claim: That only Shuayb's deniers were punished shows the event came from a freely acting creator, not the stars or nature, which would also affect his followers.
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r10.anchor: أن ذلك العذاب إنما حدث بتخليق فاعل مختار

RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r11.claim: The selective punishment shows its cause knows every particular and can distinguish obedient people from disobedient ones.
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r11.anchor: يدل على أن ذلك الفاعل المختار

RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r12.claim: Punishing some people but not others in the same town is a great miracle proving Shuayb's truth.
RAZI-FULL:v14p148/r12.anchor: يدل على المعجز العظيم في حق شعيب

RAZI-FULL:v14p149/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p149/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p149/r1.claim: Repeating 'those who denied Shuayb' intensifies their humiliation and the dreadful punishment they deserved; Arabs repeat for emphasis.
RAZI-FULL:v14p149/r1.anchor: وإنما كرر قوله : { الذين كذبوا شعيبا } لتعظيم المذلة لهم

RAZI-FULL:v14p149/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p149/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p149/r2.claim: The repeated clause also reverses the chiefs' claim: those who refused to follow Shuayb were the actual losers.
RAZI-FULL:v14p149/r2.anchor: لما قالوا : { لئن اتبعتم شعيبا إنكم إذا لخاسرون } بين تعالى أن الذين لم يتبعوه
